message.content: At a pressure of 10 kPa (≈0.1 atm) the freezing (melting) point of ordinary ice (ice I) is only slightly below 0 °C.  It drops to roughly **–0.1 °C** (about –0.075 °C by a more precise calculation).  In other words, water freezes at just a few‑tenths of a degree below the standard 0 °C point when the pressure is reduced to 10 kPa.
